A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SwallowCode and SwallowMath study. The main text, figures, tables, prompts and appendices are readable, and retained experiments can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v3 reports original continual-pretraining results, including 13 code ablations, two math experiments and an MBPP error analysis.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds Qwen2-7B experiments, an alternative training mixture, GSM-Plus evaluation and corpus diagnostics.

M1.justification: The syntax filtering, pylint filtering, SGCR, SCOR and mathematical rewriting procedures remain unchanged, including their prompts. Newly documented output exclusions and expanded two-stage rationale do not establish a procedural revision.

E1.justification: v4 adds GSM-Plus evaluation as a post-cutoff mathematical test in Appendix H.2. The original training sources, Python focus and benchmark suites remain; the alternative mixture reuses existing data sources.

E2.justification: The original corpus baselines and pipeline-variant comparisons are retained. The added Qwen2 and GSM-Plus experiments reuse Stack-Edu and Finemath-4+, respectively; Qwen2 serves as an additional training backbone.

E3.justification: v4 adds a 50B-token English-heavy mixture experiment and a controlled 20B-token Qwen2-7B comparison using learning rate 1e-5, batch size 1,024 and sequence length 4,096 (Appendices A.5 and B). It also introduces a 100,000-sample syntax audit. Section 3.1 changes the reported code-evaluation framework from BigCodeBench to EvalPlus, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 substantially expands robustness and diagnostic coverage through language-mixture and backbone checks, token-retention measurements, post-rewriting syntax-error analysis, mathematical contamination checks and GSM-Plus testing. The original MBPP analysis remains. The LLM quality-score distribution diagnostic shown in v3 Figure 8 is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v4's added analyses also report point estimates without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in v3 Tables 6-20 match v4 Tables 9-23. New results include Qwen2 HumanEval/HumanEval+ scores of 49.6/44.6 versus Stack-Edu's 39.3/34.3, GSM-Plus scores of 46.52 versus 35.75, English-heavy mixture scores, token lengths and syntax-error rates of 0.73% after SGCR and 0.46% after SCOR. These are additional findings, not improvements from rerunning the original settings. The earlier quality-score distribution results are removed.

T1.justification: Both versions are empirical dataset studies without formal theorems or proofs. v4 introduces no substantive mathematical definition or derivation; its cost extrapolation is qualitative interpretation.

C1.justification: The central contribution and headline code/math improvement claims remain. v4 explicitly extends the claimed applicability beyond Llama through Qwen2 evidence and adds claims that reusable rewritten corpora can offset their initial construction cost.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive arguments about backbone saturation, language-mixture effects, syntax-error accumulation, instruction drift in combined prompts and amortizing rewriting costs. Appendix H extends contamination interpretations to mathematics and the rewriting model, while Appendix G.4 extrapolates baseline performance beyond the tested 50B tokens. The earlier MBPP explanation and principal limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 already supplies extensive hyperparameters, software/hardware specifications, prompts, compute estimates and release links. v4 adds settings for the new experiments, documents rejection of overlong or unextractable rewritten outputs, and clarifies that syntax and pylint filtering use CPUs. These extend existing documentation rather than establish a newly available pipeline.

R1.justification: v4 substantially expands positioning against Rephrasing the Web, Nemotron-CC and MegaMath, distinguishing their formats and objectives from its rewriting approach. It also frames the contribution around undisclosed frontier-model training corpora, citing Qwen3 and DeepSeek-V3. The separate open-code-corpora subsection disappears, although its principal Stack references remain.

P1.justification: The introduction and conclusion are substantially rewritten, related work is reorganized, and the appendix narrative gains dedicated generalizability and contamination sections. Ethics, reproducibility and LLM-use statements are added, alongside author/header edits and conversion to author-year citations.

P2.justification: v4 clarifies benchmark/metric axis labels in Figures 1 and 3-5, adds three compact tables and removes v3's quality-score histogram. Template styling and float placement change, while retained pipeline, mixture, MBPP and experiment diagrams remain identical and the large ablation tables preserve their structure.

improvement.justification: The controlled Qwen2 comparison and new corpus diagnostics strengthen generalizability evidence and transparency beyond v3. The gain is limited by interpretive overreach: the mixture experiment changes several factors simultaneously, and post-cutoff performance and 50B-token curves do not establish definitive contamination exclusion or long-term cost recovery.
